faq.title: Frequently asked questions about hospital supplementary insurance
faq.subtitle: Everything about the SDK hospital plans and the IKK classic bonus.

items.q: How much does hospital supplementary insurance cost?
items.a: The premium depends on age and plan. Current examples for a 30-year-old: Klinik bei Unfall (SPU) EUR 7.00, Klinik 2-Bett (SP2) EUR 33.41 and Klinik 1-Bett (SP1) EUR 50.72 per month. The plan calculator shows your personal premium in 2 minutes.

items.q: What is the difference between Klinik 1-Bett and Klinik 2-Bett?
items.a: Klinik 1-Bett (SP1) offers accommodation in a private or twin room and a hospital daily allowance of 10 € per day. Klinik 2-Bett (SP2) offers the twin room and an upgrade option to the private-room plan from your 30th birthday, every 5 years until age 65. Both plans include chief physician treatment without GOÄ cap, free hospital choice and rooming-in.

items.q: What is the Klinik bei Unfall plan?
items.a: SPU provides the Klinik 1-Bett benefits – private or twin room, private-doctor treatment and free hospital choice – exclusively for accident-related treatment. It requires no health assessment and costs an illustrative EUR 7.00 per month for a 30-year-old.

No. SDK waives waiting periods in its hospital plans, full cover applies from the policy start date. The only requirement: the contract must be in place before treatment, as insured events that occurred before the start date are not covered.

items.q: Are private medical fees above the maximum rate reimbursed?
items.a: Yes. Reimbursement is not capped at the maximum rates of the German medical fee schedule (GOÄ). Fees beyond that are also reimbursed, a decisive point when choosing specialists.

items.q: How does the IKK classic bonus help with financing?
items.a: For recognised activities, IKK classic gives you a choice between a cash bonus and a three-times-higher subsidy for documented eligible costs. Depending on your activities, the subsidy can cover a large part of the premium and, for the accident plan, even up to 100%. The calculator on this page shows your result.

items.q: Does the cover also apply to children?
items.a: Yes, the hospital plans are available to everyone with statutory health insurance, including children. Rooming-in is part of the benefits: one parent stays with the child in hospital.

Yes, as is usual for hospital plans, the application includes health questions. That is why the best time to sign up is while you are healthy and active. You see the questions transparently in the online application.

items.q: Who benefits most from hospital supplementary insurance?
items.a: Everyone who wants freedom of choice when it matters: athletes and active people (also via the affordable accident plan), self-employed people who need to get back on their feet quickly, and families who want to stay with their child. The requirement is statutory health insurance.

neugeborene.subtitle: If you take out the hospital tariff while still pregnant, you can add your child after birth without any health assessment: within two months, retroactive to the day of birth.
neugeborene.card1Text: For a newborn, health status does not matter. This window exists exactly once in a lifetime: it lasts two months and starts at birth.
neugeborene.card2Title: The best setting if complications arise
neugeborene.card2Text: Premature birth, jaundice treatment, transfer to neonatology: if complications occur after birth, your child has the tariff's full scope of care from the start, including choice of hospital and specialists.
neugeborene.card3Text: If your child needs inpatient treatment, one parent is admitted as an accompanying person. Accommodation and meals are covered by the tariff (rooming-in).
neugeborene.requirement: Requirement: one parent is insured at the time of birth. The SDK hospital tariffs have no waiting periods, so signing up during pregnancy still makes sense, above all for your child.

faq.title: The key questions before you choose

items.q: What is the difference between SP1, SP2 and SPU?
items.a: SP1 offers a private or twin room and additional benefits such as a EUR 10 hospital allowance. SP2 covers a twin room. Both apply within the agreed scope for illness and accidents. SPU covers hospital extras only after an accident.

items.q: Is SPU full hospital supplementary insurance?
items.a: SPU provides extensive hospital extras, but only for accident-related treatment. It does not pay for hospital stays caused by illness. In return, the plan requires no health assessment.
The SDK hospital plans have no policy waiting periods. Cover applies to new insured events from the start date. An insured event that occurred before then is not covered.

items.q: Do I need to answer health questions?
items.a: The SP1 and SP2 applications include health questions. SPU requires no health assessment, but only pays after an accident. Binding acceptance takes place in the application.

items.q: Can a health fund bonus offset the entire premium?
items.a: Up to 100% premium relief is possible. This is especially tangible with affordable SPU: if your actually usable bonus at least matches your annual premium, the model can leave no effective remaining premium. Your personal amount depends on your health insurer, activities, proof and bonus terms.
If one parent is insured at the time of birth and the policy requirements are met, the child can be registered within two months without a health assessment, backdated to the day of birth.
